step0.lead: Next we cover prerequisites (Dolibarr Cron module, PHP, security key), Knot jobs, the hosting URL, and the rest. When we finish, Knot Settings opens for the engine and deeper health checks.
step0.serverHint: On the server, Knot relies on PHP and the extensions verified in Prerequisites — nothing else is required for production.
step0.ol1Desc: The Prerequisites step verifies Dolibarr’s Scheduled tasks (cron) module, PHP extensions, and (for admins) the CRON_KEY required for the public URL.
step0.ol2Desc: In Knot Settings finish the PHP wizard if needed and ensure the engine is enabled (Finish button / engine options).
step0.ol3Title: 📅 Enable Knot scheduled tasks in Dolibarr
step0.ol3Desc: The Knot jobs step lets you enable everything with one click (same as Knot Settings). Also ensure CRON_DISABLE_JOBS does not block the global scheduler.
step0.ol4Desc: Dolibarr scheduled tasks run only when something hits the public cron URL roughly every five minutes — Plesk task, crontab, HTTP service, etc. The URL to copy is on the Cron step and also in Knot Settings.

step1.title: 📋 Dolibarr & PHP prerequisites
step1.intro: These checks avoid dead ends later (missing jobs, impossible cron URL, missing extensions).
step1.cronModuleLead: It must be enabled to register Knot jobs in the database.
step1.phpOk: curl, dom, json, mbstring, openssl, simplexml are loaded.
step1.phpMissingSuffix: — enable these on your host (often php.ini or OS packages).
step1.cronKeyUnknown: Only a Dolibarr administrator can verify this key; you may still continue. The public cron URL appears later when you have the rights.
step1.cronKeyOk: A key is configured — the Cron step can display the hosting URL.
step1.cronKeyMissing: Set the key under Home → Setup → Security (cron section); otherwise no signed URL is available.
step1.fixHint: Fix the failed items above before enabling Knot tasks — but you may still step forward if you plan to configure later.

step2.title: ⚙️ Knot scheduled tasks in Dolibarr
step2.intro: Knot registers multiple jobs (worker, retention, health). They must be active in the Dolibarr scheduler for automatic workflows.
step2.globalDisabledWarn: The global scheduler looks disabled (CRON_DISABLE_JOBS). Fix Dolibarr configuration before enabling Knot rows.
step2.noneRegisteredLead: No Knot tasks are registered. Re-enable the module or open Knot Settings after installation.
step2.jobsEnabledHint: All registered rows are Active. You can also verify them inside Dolibarr.
step2.jobsDisabledHint: Use the button below to enable inactive rows (same action as Enable in Knot Settings).

step3.title: 🗓️ Scheduling & Dolibarr cron.
step3.intro: The Knot engine and other scheduled tasks only run while the Dolibarr scheduler executes when HTTP (or CLI) triggers cron regularly.
step3.needCronKey: Set CRON_KEY in Dolibarr security so the hosted URL appears below (see Prerequisites).
step3.urlHeading: URL to share with hosting (about every five minutes)
step3.urlIntro: Add this URL to a Scheduled task (Plesk, cPanel, OVH, …) or a service performing GET requests. The shown login matches Dolibarr’s parameter; share the URL only with trusted tools.
step3.crontabExample: Linux crontab example, every five minutes:
step3.curlEquivalent: You can replace wget with curl -fsS if wget is unavailable.
step3.urlMissingExplain: The URL cannot be displayed here — often missing a cron security key under Dolibarr Configuration → Security or limited admin rights.
step3.urlRecoverHint: You can retrieve it via Home → Tools → Sysinfo or the cron section of Dolibarr, or Knot Settings after this assistant.
step3.sshCliBody: With shell access schedule Dolibarr’s PHP cron runner using your hosting PHP CLI binary (example /opt/plesk/php/8.2/bin/php) targeting …/htdocs/cron_run_jobs_by_url.php or cron_run_jobs.php per Dolibarr documentation.
step3.cronExplainGlobalBlocked: The global scheduler looks disabled (CRON_DISABLE_JOBS or equivalent). Fix Dolibarr configuration then
step3.cronExplainNeedsJobs: Return to Knot jobs and activate all rows, then refresh.
step3.cronExplainPending: Jobs are enabled in Dolibarr. Configure the URL above at your hosting; the green badge appears shortly after cron runs.
step3.cronExplainOk: The Dolibarr scheduler recently executed at least one Knot job.

step4.title: 🛡️ Dolibarr permissions.
step4.intro: Knot adds five granular rights you assign from Dolibarr. Nothing ships beyond admins by default.
step4.rightsRenewHint: Disable and enable the Knot module to re-register them.

step5.title: 🔐 Credential encryption.
step5.intro: Knot encrypts all credentials with AES-256-GCM derived from Dolibarr’s unique instance fingerprint.
step5.backupExplain: Keep regular SQL dumps of conf.php — losing the Dolibarr identifier makes ciphertext unreadable.
step5.encryptionFix: $dolibarr_main_instance_unique_id is empty in conf.php. Generate it via Dolibarr (Configuration → Security) before relying on encrypted credentials.

step6.intro: Starter templates sometimes send invoices. Knot reuses Dolibarr’s SMTP settings — nothing to duplicate.
step6.smtpOkDetail: You can already use connector action.email with a dedicated SMTP credential.
step6.smtpMissingDetail: Configure SMTP under Dolibarr Configuration → Email, then create a Knot SMTP credential. You can skip and return later.

step7.intro: Five pre-wired drafts covering frequent use cases — imported disabled with schedules off. Customize as needed.
step7.importedBanner: {count} templates imported. Find them under Workflows as drafts.
